labels.swarmItem: File: /workspace/lab/QueryProcessing/select.cpp (final variant: /workspace/agent_tmp/select.final.cpp). Implement `int select(Buffer *buf)` — selection over R and S. STAGE 1 (selection_scan_r): start with pushToWrite(buf, NULL, 0, SELECT_RET_ADDR, true) to reset the output stream; then the R branch: for addr 0..15, blk = readBlockFromDisk(addr, buf); decode with readTuplesFromBlock into Relation t[TUPLE_PER_BLK]; for each tuple with attr1 == 40: print it via `cout << t[i].attr1 << " " << t[i].attr2 << endl;` and pushToWrite(buf, (unsigned char*)&t[i], sizeof(Relation), SELECT_RET_ADDR); then freeBlockInBuffer(blk, buf). Leave the S branch and final flush as a marked TODO stub, return 0. STAGE 2 (selection_operator, only in final variant): add the S branch — identical loop over blocks 16..47 keeping tuples with attr1 == 60 (S.C = 60), same print/pushToWrite pattern; then finish with pushToWrite(buf, NULL, 0, SELECT_RET_ADDR, false, true) to flush the tail block; return 0. `using namespace std;` is already present.

File: /workspace/lab/QueryProcessing/mergeSort.cpp (final variant: /workspace/agent_tmp/mergeSort.final.cpp). Implement `int mergeSort(Buffer *buf, bool choice)` — two-pass external merge sort. choice==SORT_R: sort relation R (blocks 0..15) by attr1; runs to MERGE_R_SEG_ADDR(10000), final sorted output to MERGE_R_RET_ADDR(11000), 16 output blocks. choice==SORT_S: S (blocks 16..47), runs to MERGE_S_SEG_ADDR(12000), output to MERGE_S_RET_ADDR(13000), 32 blocks. Sort key: attr1, tie-break attr2 (deterministic). STAGE 1 (external_sort_runs): pass 1 only. M = buf->numAllBlk (8). For each run i of up to M consecutive input blocks: read each block with readBlockFromDisk, decode with readTuplesFromBlock into a memory array (Relation run[M*TUPLE_PER_BLK]), freeBlockInBuffer each block immediately after decoding (hold at most 1 slot); std::sort the run; then write the run's blocks to segAddr + i*M + j — build each 64-byte block in a local memory buffer (7 sorted tuples, 4 zero bytes, next-pointer at offset 60: +1 within the run, 0 at the run's last block), then getNewBlockInBuffer + memcpy + writeBlockToDisk per block. After pass 1, stage-1 ends with `/* TODO: pass 2 (multi-way merge) */` and return 0. STAGE 2 (external_merge_sort, only in the final variant): k-way merge of the k = ceil(blkNum/M) runs (k <= 4). Hold one buffer slot per run: current block addr per run starts at segAddr + i*M; decode its tuples; repeatedly pick the run whose current tuple is smallest (attr1, then attr2), append that tuple to a memory output array; when 7 accumulate, write one output block to retAddr + outBlk++ (next-pointer at offset 60 = retAddr+outBlk, except the very last output block gets 0 — total tuple count is known: R_NUM or S_NUM) via a local memory block + getNewBlockInBuffer + writeBlockToDisk; advance the run's position, and when its block is exhausted follow the next-pointer at offset 60 to read the next block (freeing the old slot; next==0 means run exhausted — free its slot and skip it). Return 0. Static helper functions inside the file are fine. Includes already present: iostream, string.h, algorithm, cmath, mergeSort.h, file.h, blkio.h.

File: /workspace/lab/QueryProcessing/hashJoin.cpp (final variant: /workspace/agent_tmp/hashJoin.final.cpp). Implement `int hashJoin(Buffer *buf)` — hash join on R.A = S.C. STAGE 1 (hash_partitioning): phase 1 only. Partition R: pushHashToWrite(buf, NULL, HASH_R_ADDR, true) to reset; for blocks 0..15: readBlockFromDisk, readTuplesFromBlock, pushHashToWrite(buf, &t[i], HASH_R_ADDR) per tuple, freeBlockInBuffer; then pushHashToWrite(buf, NULL, HASH_R_ADDR, false, true). Partition S identically over blocks 16..47 with HASH_S_ADDR. Leave phase 2 as a marked TODO stub, return 0. STAGE 2 (hash_join, only in final variant): first pushToWrite(buf, NULL, 0, HJ_RET_ADDR, true). Then for each bucket b in 0..BUCKET_NUM-1: (a) load R's bucket b fully into a memory array Relation rBuf[R_NUM]: walk the chain from HASH_R_ADDR + b*100 — blk = readBlockFromDisk(addr, buf); rCount += readHashFromBlock(blk, rBuf + rCount); read next-chain pointer at `*(int*)(blk + HASH_PER_BLK * sizeof(Relation) + sizeof(int))` (offset 52); freeBlockInBuffer(blk, buf); continue while next != 0. (b) stream S's bucket b the same way block-by-block (decode into Relation sBuf[HASH_PER_BLK]); for each S tuple, scan rBuf[0..rCount) for equal attr1 and emit each match via output(buf, HJ_RET_ADDR, r.attr1, r.attr2, s.attr2) — i.e. (A, B, D); free each S block and follow its offset-52 chain pointer. After all buckets: pushToWrite(buf, NULL, 0, HJ_RET_ADDR, false, true); return 0. Buffer discipline: at most 1 slot held at any time plus transient flush slot.

File: /workspace/lab/QueryProcessing/project.cpp (final variant: /workspace/agent_tmp/project.final.cpp). Implement `int project(Buffer *buf)` — projection of R onto A with duplicate elimination. STAGE 1 (projection_prepare): call mergeSort(buf, SORT_R) (mergeSort.h is already included) to produce sorted R at MERGE_R_RET_ADDR(11000); then pushToWrite(buf, NULL, 0, PROJECT_RET_ADDR, true) to reset the projection output stream; declare whatever locals you need; leave the scan as a marked TODO stub and return 0. STAGE 2 (projection_operator, only in final variant): scan the 16 sorted R blocks at MERGE_R_RET_ADDR..MERGE_R_RET_ADDR+15: per block readBlockFromDisk + readTuplesFromBlock; emit attr1 only when it differs from the previously emitted value (emit the very first tuple's attr1): print `cout << t[i].attr1 << endl;` and pushToWrite(buf, (unsigned char*)&t[i].attr1, sizeof(int), PROJECT_RET_ADDR); freeBlockInBuffer each block after use. End with pushToWrite(buf, NULL, 0, PROJECT_RET_ADDR, false, true); return 0.

File: /workspace/lab/QueryProcessing/nestedLoopJoin.cpp (final variant: /workspace/agent_tmp/nestedLoopJoin.final.cpp). Implement `int nestedLoopJoin(Buffer *buf)` — block nested-loop join on R.A = S.C with M = buf->numAllBlk (8) buffer slots. Start with pushToWrite(buf, NULL, 0, NLJ_RET_ADDR, true). STAGE 1 (nested_loop_outer_scan): the outer loop only: iterate over R in groups of M-1 = 7 blocks (base = 0; base < R_BLK_NUM; base += M-1): read up to 7 consecutive R blocks with readBlockFromDisk, decode each into a memory array (e.g. Relation rBuf[7][TUPLE_PER_BLK]) and KEEP the 7 pool slots held during the inner phase (store the block pointers); leave the inner S scan as a marked TODO stub inside the group loop; after the (stubbed) inner phase, freeBlockInBuffer each held R block. return 0. STAGE 2 (nested_loop_join, only in final variant): fill in the inner probe: for s in S_ADDR..S_ADDR+S_BLK_NUM-1: sBlk = readBlockFromDisk(s, buf) (this is the 8th slot); decode sT[7]; collect all matches between the held R blocks' tuples and sT (r.attr1 == s.attr1) into a memory array Relation3 matches[7*TUPLE_PER_BLK*TUPLE_PER_BLK] with fields (r.attr1, r.attr2, s.attr2); then freeBlockInBuffer(sBlk, buf) BEFORE emitting; then emit each collected match via output(buf, NLJ_RET_ADDR, m.attr1, m.attr2, m.attr3) — emitting after freeing the S block guarantees a free slot for pushToWrite's transient flush. After all groups: pushToWrite(buf, NULL, 0, NLJ_RET_ADDR, false, true); return 0.

File: /workspace/lab/QueryProcessing/sortMergeJoin.cpp (final variant: /workspace/agent_tmp/sortMergeJoin.final.cpp). Implement `int sortMergeJoin(Buffer *buf)` — sort-merge join on R.A = S.C. STAGE 1 (sort_merge_preparation): call mergeSort(buf, SORT_R) and mergeSort(buf, SORT_S) (mergeSort.h already included) producing sorted R at MERGE_R_RET_ADDR(11000, 16 blocks) and sorted S at MERGE_S_RET_ADDR(13000, 32 blocks); pushToWrite(buf, NULL, 0, SMJ_RET_ADDR, true); then load the first sorted R block (readBlockFromDisk(MERGE_R_RET_ADDR, buf), decode into rT[7], position rPos=0) and the first sorted S block likewise (sT[7], sPos=0) — keep both slots held; declare the state you need; leave the merge scan as a marked TODO stub, return 0. STAGE 2 (sort_merge_join, only in final variant): classic two-pointer merge with duplicate-key groups, holding at most one R block and one S block slot at a time: if rT[rPos].attr1 < sT[sPos].attr1 advance R; if greater advance S; on equality with key k: collect the full R group (all consecutive tuples with attr1==k, advancing across R blocks as needed) into a memory array rg[R_NUM] and the full S group into sg[S_NUM], then emit the cross product via output(buf, SMJ_RET_ADDR, k, rg[i].attr2, sg[j].attr2) for all pairs. Advancing a cursor: pos++; when pos reaches TUPLE_PER_BLK, read the chain next-pointer at offset 60 of the held block, freeBlockInBuffer it, and if next != 0 readBlockFromDisk(next) + decode + pos=0, else that side is exhausted (mark with a flag/invalid addr). Loop while both sides unexhausted. After the scan free any still-held blocks, then pushToWrite(buf, NULL, 0, SMJ_RET_ADDR, false, true); return 0.

File: /workspace/lab/QueryOptimize/tree.cpp (final variant: /workspace/agent_tmp/tree.final.cpp). Implement `void TreeNode::preOrder(int level)` (class in tree.h: type is one of SELECT/PROJECTION/JOIN/LEAF, plus info, left, right). STAGE 1 (query_tree_node_output): node formatting only: print level*4 spaces of indentation (level groups of 4 spaces), then: if type == "LEAF" print info; else if info is empty print type; else print `type + " [ " + info + " ]"`; end with newline. Leave recursion out (marked TODO comment). STAGE 2 (query_tree, only in final variant): after printing the current node, recurse: if (left) left->preOrder(level + 1); if (right) right->preOrder(level + 1); Use std::cout (iostream is included; no `using namespace std;` in this file — qualify with std::).

File: /workspace/lab/QueryOptimize/main.cpp (final variant: /workspace/agent_tmp/mainopt.final.cpp). Implement the two hollowed functions in this file (read it first; main() is already complete and must stay byte-identical — only fill in parseQuery and optimizeQuery; helper static functions above them are allowed). STAGE 1 (query_parser): `void parseQuery(TreeNode *root, string query)` — recursive-descent parse of relational-algebra strings into a tree hung at root->left. Token types: keywords SELECT / PROJECTION / JOIN, identifiers (relation names), '[', ']', '(', ')'. Grammar: expr := ('SELECT'|'PROJECTION') '[' info ']' '(' expr ')' | operand ( 'JOIN' operand )* where operand := '(' expr ')' | IDENT. Build: SELECT/PROJECTION node with info = trimmed text between brackets, child in ->left; JOIN node with ->left/->right operands (left-associative for chains); relation names become TreeNode("LEAF", name). Suggested structure: a static helper `static TreeNode *parseExpr(const string &s, size_t &pos)` with skip-whitespace and word-reading helpers; parseQuery just sets root->left = parseExpr(...). Sample inputs (from main()): "SELECT [ ENAME = 'Mary' & DNAME = 'Research' ] ( EMPLOYEE JOIN DEPARTMENT )", "PROJECTION [ BDATE ] ( SELECT [ ENAME = 'John' & DNAME = 'Research' ] ( EMPLOYEE JOIN DEPARTMENT ) )", "SELECT [ ESSN = '01' ] ( PROJECTION [ ESSN, PNAME ] ( WORKS_ON JOIN PROJECT ) )". STAGE 1 leaves `optimizeQuery` as the existing `return root;` stub. STAGE 2 (query_optimizer, only in final variant): `TreeNode *optimizeQuery(TreeNode *root, vector<string> info)` — heuristic predicate pushdown; `info` carries predicates (already split, trimmed) pushed down from ancestors. Rules: root==NULL -> return NULL. SELECT: split root->info on '&', trim each part, append to a copy of info, return optimizeQuery(root->left, that) (the SELECT node itself is dissolved). PROJECTION: root->left = optimizeQuery(root->left, info); return root (predicates pass through). JOIN: partition info into leftPreds/rightPreds/keep — a predicate belongs to a side if its attribute name (first token before whitespace or '=') shares its first character with the name of a LEAF under that subtree and with no LEAF under the other subtree (helper to collect LEAF info strings of a subtree); unmatched predicates stay in keep. Recurse root->left = optimizeQuery(root->left, leftPreds), root->right = optimizeQuery(root->right, rightPreds), then wrap the keep predicates as a SELECT chain above the JOIN: iterate keep from last to first, each step node = new TreeNode("SELECT", pred) with node->left = previous node (start from root), so the earliest predicate ends up outermost; return the chain top. LEAF: wrap ALL of info as such a SELECT chain above the leaf (same last-to-first construction) and return the top (if info empty return root). Expected results: query1 optimizes to JOIN(SELECT[ENAME = 'Mary']->EMPLOYEE, SELECT[DNAME = 'Research']->DEPARTMENT); query2 keeps PROJECTION on top of that same optimized join; query3 becomes PROJECTION -> SELECT[ESSN = '01'] -> JOIN(WORKS_ON, PROJECT) since ESSN matches neither W nor P. Verify both variants with `g++ -std=c++17 -fsyntax-only -I/workspace/lab/QueryOptimize <path>`.

lastPrompt: This project implements two undergraduate database-lab components: (1) an external-memory relational query processing system and (2) a query-tree optimisation engine. Both are C++ applications built with CMake. The query processing system operates on two simulated relations R(A,B) (112 tuples, 16 blocks) and S(C,D) (224 tuples, 32 blocks) stored as fixed-size 64-byte block files in `/workspace/lab/QueryProcessing/data/`. A fixed-size buffer (520 bytes, holding up to 8 blocks) provides block-level I/O primitives; all operators must respect this constraint. The compiled binary at `/[redacted]` accepts interactive commands: `select`, `project`, `nlj`, `hj`, `smj`. The query optimiser parses textual query representations into tree structures and applies heuristic transformations (predicate pushdown). Its binary is at `/[redacted]`. Your working directory is `/workspace`. The project code is already present. You need to implement all the modules and features listed below so that all tests pass. Implement the following hollowed units: Buffer Initialization (`lab/QueryProcessing/extmem.cpp`): implement `initBuffer`, allocating the buffer memory region and setting the core metadata fields. Buffer Block Allocation (`lab/QueryProcessing/extmem.cpp`): implement `getNewBlockInBuffer`, selecting a free slot and returning its payload pointer. Buffer Block Release (`lab/QueryProcessing/extmem.cpp`): implement `freeBlockInBuffer`, returning a consumed slot to the free list. Buffer Block Read (`lab/QueryProcessing/extmem.cpp`): implement `readBlockFromDisk`, loading a numbered block file into an available buffer slot. Buffer Block Write (`lab/QueryProcessing/extmem.cpp`): implement `writeBlockToDisk`, flushing a buffer slot back to disk and releasing it. Buffered Tuple Writer (`lab/QueryProcessing/blkio.cpp`): implement `pushToWrite`, batching result tuples into output blocks with reset/push controls. Tuple Block Decoder (`lab/QueryProcessing/blkio.cpp`): implement `readTuplesFromBlock`, deserialising raw relation blocks into `Relation` tuples. Join Output Emitter (`lab/QueryProcessing/blkio.cpp`): implement `output`, printing 3-attribute join tuples and forwarding them to disk output. Hash Partition Writer (`lab/QueryProcessing/blkio.cpp`): implement `pushHashToWrite`, routing tuples into hash buckets on disk. Hash Partition Reader (`lab/QueryProcessing/blkio.cpp`): implement `readHashFromBlock`, decoding bucket records back into relation tuples. Query Tree Node Output (`lab/QueryOptimize/tree.cpp`): implement the node-formatting portion of `TreeNode::preOrder` with 4-space indentation. Query Tree Traversal (`lab/QueryOptimize/tree.cpp`): complete `TreeNode::preOrder` by recursively traversing left and right subtrees. Query Parser (`lab/QueryOptimize/main.cpp`): implement `parseQuery`, tokenising the relational-algebra string into SELECT/PROJECTION/JOIN/LEAF nodes. Query Optimizer (`lab/QueryOptimize/main.cpp`): implement `optimizeQuery`, splitting compound predicates and pushing SELECT nodes below JOIN/PROJECTION nodes. External Sort Run Generation (`lab/QueryProcessing/mergeSort.cpp`): implement pass 1 of `mergeSort`, reading M-block segments, sorting them in memory, and writing sorted runs. External Merge Sort Final Merge (`lab/QueryProcessing/mergeSort.cpp`): implement pass 2 of `mergeSort`, merging run heads into the final globally sorted output. Selection Scan for R (`lab/QueryProcessing/select.cpp`): implement the R-side branch of `select`, filtering tuples where `A = 40`. Selection Scan for S and Final Flush (`lab/QueryProcessing/select.cpp`): complete `select` by filtering S tuples where `C = 60`, then flushing the buffered output. Projection Preparation (`lab/QueryProcessing/project.cpp`): implement the setup phase of `project`, invoking `mergeSort(buf, SORT_R)` and initialising projection output. Projection Deduplication Scan (`lab/QueryProcessing/project.cpp`): complete `project` by scanning sorted R output and emitting distinct A
